desc: Derive and prove the game-theoretic winning criterion for legal edge additions, using exhaustive small-state analysis to detect the invariant.
Analyze internal missing cross-edge moves versus component-merging moves, including the effect of the two possible bipartition orientations.
Verify the resulting criterion on all three samples and representative small graphs, preferably via exhaustive game-state enumeration.
Design an \(O(N+M)\) implementation to compute the required component summaries using BFS/DFS or parity DSU.
Produce the final Python solution with stdin parsing and `Aoki`/`Takahashi` output.
